clue.text: Serious trouble distributing weed at rep

indicators.note: distributing spreads things around, so these letters get scattered into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Handing out cannabis to a sales rep could land you in serious trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributing weed' reads like drug dealing, but it just tells you to rearrange the letters of 'weed at rep'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in deep water is an idiom for facing great difficulty or danger, like a swimmer out of their depth.

clue.text: A quip BDSM gone wrong is a letdown

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke during a kinky session that falls flat kills the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The racy surface is just a pile of letters; BDSM supplies the awkward consonants B, D, S and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A damp squib is a British idiom for an anticlimax: a firework that fails to go off because it got wet.

clue.text: County chess excellent all round

indicators.note: the surrounding words go all round the answer, enclosing it within their letters

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A county chess team that is strong in every department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' looks like praise for the players, but it tells you the answer is wrapped inside 'chESS EXcellent'. Essex is an English county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essex is one of the home counties of England, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Terribly windy pals could make bloomer

indicators.note: terribly means badly or in a disordered way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Friends with bad flatulence might commit an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, which is the sense the surface plays on; here it means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild pansy is a flowering plant, and a crossword bloomer is anything that blossoms, so this is an example.

clue.text: Used pants seen in river for period of time

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Second-hand underwear spotted floating in a river over some stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for underwear, but it is British slang for 'bad', here the anagram signal for 'used'.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week is a fixed span of twenty-four hours, so it qualifies as a stretch of time.

clue.text: Once more assesses setters in need of editing

indicators.note: text needing editing is not yet in the right order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers whose work needs correcting get checked again.
explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential joke about crossword setters needing an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something again is to evaluate or examine it a second time, matching the verb phrase.

clue.text: Bite to eat and beer outside quiet pub at front

indicators.note: being outside means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the rest

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: what is at the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A snack and a pint, bought at the front of a quiet pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ps sit together inside the beer: A(P P)LE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a piece of fruit you can take a quick snack from, so it is an example of something to eat.

clue.text: Be hesitant to dismiss female change

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to falter is to waver or hesitate
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Someone wavers over firing a woman, then makes a change.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the F from the front of the verb for hesitating leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify or adjust it, a straightforward synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Does my pun upset Serpent in the Independent?

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over and disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter worries whether a wordplay gag will annoy a fellow compiler at the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Serpent is the byline of one of the Independent's crossword setters, as Hoskins is of this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Setters publish under invented names, so the byline Serpent in that newspaper is an example of an assumed name.

clue.text: Oust leaders for evil jokes? Expect countless troubles!

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A warning that bad jokes will get you thrown out and cause endless problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation splits the source words across two sentences, but the five words run on regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject someone is to throw them out or expel them, a direct synonym for the verb.

clue.text: I'm less cut out to be pumped in the extreme!

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A gym-goer complains they are not ripped enough to look truly bulked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' and 'pumped' are both bodybuilding slang, so 'cut out' reads naturally; 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumped describes swollen bodybuilder muscles, and the superlative form expresses the most extreme degree of that.

clue.text: Those people beginning to eat a Topic?

parts.note: them refers to those people

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Some people starting to eat a Topic, the British chocolate bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A Topic is a British chocolate bar with nougat and hazelnuts, which explains the capital and the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or main idea of a talk or piece of writing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Make more exciting drink to entertain old flame

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes guests in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: to sup is to drink
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Livening things up by having a drink with a former lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old flame' points to a former partner by the usual short form, and 'to entertain' means the drink takes that piece in.
explanation.definitionFit: To sex up a report or story is informal for making it more appealing or sensational.

clue.text: Insult conservative and socialist relations in disgrace

parts.note: to dis is slang for to insult
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a red is a left-winger
it is a coy word for sex, i.e. sexual relations

explanation.surface: A slanging match between left and right brings both sides into shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' here means sexual relations, for which 'it' is the old euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Discredit as a noun means loss of reputation or standing, a synonym for shame or dishonour.

clue.text: A French servant with large yen to be feminine?

parts.note: un is French for a
a man is a manservant
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A French valet with a strong desire to seem womanly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like longing, but it is the Japanese currency, abbreviated to its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanly means lacking traditionally masculine qualities, so the question mark flags a loose equivalence with womanly.

clue.text: Crooked man stashing police record with diamonds

indicators.note: to stash is to hide away inside something, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a man is a male
form is British slang for a criminal record
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A dishonest man hides his criminal past along with stolen jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' suggests dishonesty, but here it means bent out of shape. 'Form' is British slang for previous convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something malformed is badly shaped or twisted, like a bent or misshapen object.

clue.text: Class religious academy cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims off its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a seminary trains priests

explanation.surface: A lesson at a theological college ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the final Y from the college for priests leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small teaching group at a university, a kind of lesson or tutorial session.

clue.text: People who will pass on fashionable blaspheming?

definitions.note: a gerund standing for a noun: blaspheming is an example of such a sin

parts.note: humans are mortal: they will pass away
in means trendy

explanation.surface: Folk who pass judgement on trendy swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' reads as 'comment on', but 'pass' means die and 'on' just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Catholic teaching a grave offence against God, such as speaking sacrilegiously, damns the soul; the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Soldiers first to nose a perfume that's reviving

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: the first part of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter
taken as written
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: Troops are first to sniff a restorative fragrance, like smelling salts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers (RE) are a regular crossword source for 'soldiers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn or coming back to life, so it matches the adjective for regaining vigour.

clue.text: Sailor's ceased to have sex, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: to be laid is slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A sailor admits they have given up their love life.
explanation.walkthrough: Belay is a nautical command meaning stop, hence the sailor in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: On ships, 'belay that' means stop, so in a sailor's vocabulary the past tense means halted or stopped.

clue.text: Help up rocker's foe cut by head of nasty Stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the order flips

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: something cut by another is split open with that piece inserted

parts.note: mods and rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Help a rocker escape an attack from a vicious Rolling Stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods and rockers were rival British youth tribes of the 1960s, scooters against motorbikes. The capital on 'Stone' hints at the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond is a precious gem, so it is an example of a stone in the jewellery sense.

clue.text: One rowing over a vacuous rebellious bloke

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
taken as written

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside is removed and only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: its outer letters
a bloke is a man

explanation.surface: Someone arguing with an empty-headed troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rowing' wants to rhyme with 'cow', a British word for quarrelling; here it rhymes with 'go' and means using oars. In cricket, an over is six balls, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oarsman is a person who propels a boat with oars, so he is someone who is rowing.

clue.text: Monster joints picked up in Scottish islands

indicators.note: picked up as on a radio, meaning heard, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: an orc is a monster, and knees are joints

explanation.surface: Bones of a sea monster discovered on remote Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcs are the monsters of Tolkien; their knees, said quickly, give the island group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orkneys are an archipelago off the north coast of mainland Scotland.

clue.text: A job detaining out-of-head violent type?

definitions.text: A job detaining out-of-head violent type?

indicators.note: detaining someone holds them in, so one piece goes inside another
with the head out, the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a task is a job
a tough is a thug

explanation.surface: Holding a drugged-up thug in custody is a hard assignment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a thug off their head would be hard to detain. The headless thug, OUGH, goes inside the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough ask is an idiom for a demanding request, and restraining a violent person is exactly such a demand.

clue.text: Use a face covering in conversation

indicators.note: conversation is spoken, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a veil covers the face

explanation.surface: Wearing a mask or veil while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' looks like a verb going with 'a face covering', but it stands alone as a noun: of no avail means of no use.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means benefit or usefulness, as in the phrase to no avail.

clue.text: Enter office or come home?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: be elected to power
second meaning: arrive back at your house

explanation.walkthrough: 'Enter office' reads like walking into a workplace, but means winning an election, as a party does at the polls.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both being elected to government and arriving back at your house in the evening.

clue.text: Swedish band finally entertains Algerian leader

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes guests in, so one piece is included with another

parts.note: ABBA were the Swedish pop group

indicators.note: finally points at the end of a word, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A Swedish pop group ends up performing for a North African head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferhat Abbas led Algeria's provisional government during its war of independence. 'Entertains' does double duty: its last letter follows the band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferhat Abbas was president of the Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic, so he is an example.

clue.text: Do nothing to support British fire

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so this piece is placed below the other

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to laze is to idle

explanation.surface: Refusing to back the British firing line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the idling comes after B.
explanation.definitionFit: A blaze is a large fierce fire, a direct synonym for the noun.

clue.text: Lawyer rejected Cambridge university grant

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a DA is a US district attorney
MIT is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A law graduate turned down for a scholarship at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge university' pulls toward England, but it is the Cambridge in Massachusetts, home of MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant a point is to concede or acknowledge it, which is what admitting it means.

clue.text: Exaggerate about gallery pinching original of Sickert

parts.note: over means about, as in arguing over money

indicators.note: the original is the first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Overplaying the story of a London gallery stealing a Sickert painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Sickert was a British painter. The gallery grabs the S and holds it just in front of itself rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to express something too strongly, which is the same as exaggerating it.

clue.text: Loaded nurse chasing after young man

indicators.note: a chaser comes behind, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: a lad is a young man
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A drunk nurse pursues a younger man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' suggests drunk or rich, but here means weighed down. EN is an enrolled nurse in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means heavily burdened or carrying a cargo, the same as weighed down.

clue.text: Get rid of all bad bits in Dent sci-fi novel

definitions.text: Get rid of all bad bits

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take on a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Edit out every weak passage in a science-fiction book by someone called Dent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book, but it is the anagram signal; 'bad bits' are germs, not poor passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinfecting kills harmful germs and bacteria, cleaning a surface of the nasty microbes on it.
